title: Restoring a two-stage population
stem: A nursery models juvenile and adult plants by $v_{n+1}=Lv_n$, where $L=\begin{pmatrix}0&f\\0.5&0.5\end{pmatrix}$. Initially $v_0=(160,100)^T$, and $v_1=(80,130)^T$. No plants enter from outside. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine $f$ and interpret both entries of the second row.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the eigenvalues and decide whether this model sustains the population in the long term.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the adult-to-juvenile ratio approached by a non-zero population. Explain why a negative eigenvalue does not mean negative plant numbers.

steps.text: Half the juveniles become adults and half the existing adults survive to the next year.
The dominant modulus is below 1, so the population tends to zero.
The negative eigenvalue describes an alternating decaying component; non-negative initial data remain non-negative under $L$.

title: Investment returns with an early exit
stem: An investment costs 5000 now and returns 2000 at the end of each of years 1, 2 and 3. Its net present value at annual rate $r$ is the discounted receipts less 5000. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the net present value at 8% and at 10%.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Estimate the annual rate for which the net present value is zero, and explain why there is only one positive solution.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A buyer offers 3500 immediately after the first receipt. At an 8% discount rate, decide whether selling is preferable to retaining the remaining receipts.

steps.text: Each positive receipt decreases as the discount rate increases, so $N$ is strictly decreasing for $r>0$.
At year 1, the remaining receipts have value $2000/1.08+2000/1.08^2$.
This is 3566.53, exceeding 3500; retaining has the higher present value.

stem: A sensor reading is represented by $(x,1)^T$. A gain operation is $G=\begin{pmatrix}1.2&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and an offset is $H=\begin{pmatrix}1&10\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. steps.text: For column vectors the operation performed first is on the right.
Gain then offset gives 106; offset then gain gives 108.
The first coordinate differs by 2 for every $(x,1)^T$; there is no such reading.

title: Reconstructing two original mixtures
stem: A mixing process sends 70% of tank A and 20% of tank B into tank C. The rest enters tank D. Final volumes are 40 litres in C and 60 litres in D. No liquid is lost. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use a matrix inverse to determine the original volumes.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Only C is measured with an error: its recorded volume increases by $\varepsilon$ while D stays 60. Find the errors in the recovered volumes.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why a much smaller determinant could make this reconstruction less reliable.

steps.text: The determinant is 0.5, so the inverse exists.
Errors are $1.6\varepsilon$ in A and $-0.6\varepsilon$ in B.
The inverse divides by the determinant.
For otherwise comparable entries, measurement errors can be magnified substantially.

title: Combining two out-of-phase signals
stem: Two signals are $u(t)=8\cos(30t)$ and $v(t)=6\cos(30t+\pi/2)$. Their total is written $w(t)=R\cos(30t+\phi)$ with $R>0$ and $-\pi<\phi\le\pi$. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use complex numbers to find $R$ and $\phi$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A third signal of amplitude 5 is added. Determine the phase that minimises the resulting amplitude and find that minimum.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why no choice of the third phase makes the total signal identically zero.

steps.text: Choose the third phasor opposite to $8+6i$.
By the reverse triangle inequality, the smallest possible amplitude is $10-5=5$.
Cancellation requires equal and opposite phasors.
The existing resultant has amplitude 10 but the third has amplitude 5.

title: A spiral generated by repeated multiplication
stem: A point begins at $z_0=2$ and is updated by $z_{n+1}=1.1e^{i\pi/6}z_n$. The diagram shows only the starting point and the reference axes. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the least positive $n$ for which the point lies on the positive real axis again. Find its distance from the origin then.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the first $n$ for which the distance exceeds 10, and determine the principal argument then.

steps.text: Each update rotates anticlockwise by $\pi/6$ and enlarges distances from the origin by factor 1.1.
Require $n\pi/6$ to be a multiple of $2\pi$.

title: Recovering a quadratic from an Argand point
stem: A real monic quadratic has a root represented by the point $(2,3)$ on an Argand diagram. Its graph meets the real vertical axis at $c$. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the other root and the quadratic.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the minimum value of the real function and explain its connection to the diagram.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A vertical shift produces exactly one real root. Determine the shift.

steps.text: A real-coefficient quadratic has conjugate roots, so the other root is $2-3i$.
The positive minimum is the square of the imaginary coordinate, $3^2$; no real roots occur.
The vertex must lie on the horizontal axis.

stem: A decorative process adds disjoint patches. At stage $n\ge1$ the total area added is $3(0.4)^{n-1}$ square units, while the total new boundary length is $4(1.2)^{n-1}$ units. steps.text: The boundary series has ratio 1.2, exceeding 1.
Its terms do not tend to zero, so the boundary sum diverges despite the convergent area sum.

title: Decoding a message with one corrupted entry
stem: An encoder maps column pairs by $c=Ax+b$, with $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $b=(3,-2)^T$. A received pair is $(18,9)^T$. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Only the first received coordinate is corrupted by an additive error $e$. Find the corresponding error in the decoded pair.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Give one check on decoded data that cannot detect this corruption, and explain why.

steps.text: Checking the sum of the decoded coordinates cannot detect it.

title: When two measurements cannot identify a mixture
stem: Two unknown concentrations satisfy $2x+3y=12$ and $4x+ky=24$. A laboratory claims that two equations always determine one unique pair. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of $k$ for which the coefficient matrix is singular.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: For this value of $k$, describe all non-negative solutions and explain the laboratory’s error.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: If the second total were 25 instead of 24, with $k=6$, explain what could be concluded.

steps.text: There are infinitely many feasible pairs, since the second measurement provides no independent information.
Doubling the first equation forces the total to be 24.
A total of 25 is inconsistent; no exact solution exists and measurement/model error should be investigated.
